scope: Cumulative multiple-choice review of the uploaded Foundations, Mesopotamia, Egypt and Ancient Israel binder pages.

pool.prompt: Why does 9000 BCE come before 3500 BCE?
options: BCE years count down toward the common era
BCE years count up toward the common era
The smaller year is always older
pool.rationale: The common era is the reference point. Within BCE a larger number is farther back in time.

pool.prompt: Which two labels refer to the same calendar year?
pool.rationale: AD and CE use the same year numbering.

pool.prompt: A timeline reads “ca. 600 BCE.” Which reading fits?
options: Exactly the first day of 600 BCE
About 600 years into the common era
About 600 years before the common era
Six decades before the common era
pool.rationale: The abbreviation ca. means approximately, and BCE means before the common era.

pool.prompt: How many years are in three decades?
pool.rationale: Each decade is ten years.

pool.prompt: Which span equals one century?
pool.rationale: Ten decades of ten years each make one hundred years.

pool.prompt: A settlement grew for about 200 years. How long is that?
pool.rationale: A century lasts one hundred years, so two centuries last 200 years.

pool.prompt: Why might a hunter-gatherer group move to a different camp in winter?
options: To harvest a large field of planted grain
To move closer to a permanent pottery shop
To follow seasonal sources of food and water
To store grain in a city warehouse
pool.rationale: Nomadic hunter-gatherers moved to find available resources.

pool.prompt: At a camp, archaeologists find a hearth and a sharp stone scraper. What could those have helped people do?
options: Cook food and work animal hides
pool.rationale: Fire helps cook food, and a scraper helps work hides.

pool.prompt: A group carries hunting tools and builds temporary shelters. What does this help the group do?
options: Use different hunting areas as seasons change
Keep livestock beside the same field all year
Send taxes to one permanent city
Store a harvest in one brick building
pool.rationale: Portable equipment and temporary shelter help a mobile group adapt to changing conditions.

pool.prompt: Which example shows domestication?
options: Following a wild herd to a new valley
Raising sheep over generations for useful traits
Collecting fallen branches for a fire
Catching wild fish near a camp
pool.rationale: Domestication involves people raising and shaping plants or animals over generations.

pool.prompt: Which pairing shows resources people could use in a farming village?
options: Clay tablets for clothing and wool for walls
Barley for roof beams and bronze for food
Wool for clothing and mud brick for homes
Canal water for walls and river silt for shoes
pool.rationale: Domesticated animals supplied wool, and settled communities could build mud-brick homes.

pool.prompt: Why did planting fields often encourage permanent settlements?
options: People needed to follow wild game every day
People could move an entire field each season
People no longer needed access to water
People could stay to tend and harvest crops
pool.rationale: Remaining near fields made it easier to grow, protect, and harvest crops.

pool.prompt: A farmer swaps grain directly for a woven mat. What is this?
pool.rationale: Barter is exchanging goods or services directly.

pool.prompt: Why can a food surplus lead to more specialized jobs?
options: Extra food makes everyone farm full time
Extra food can support people whose main work is outside farming
Stored grain replaces the need for trained craftspeople
A surplus prevents people from exchanging goods
pool.rationale: A surplus can feed weavers, potters, and other specialists.

pool.prompt: A village grows extra grain and one villager becomes its full-time potter. Which idea explains that job change?
options: The start of the common era
pool.rationale: Specialization means focusing on a particular kind of work. A food surplus helps support that arrangement.

pool.prompt: Which find best supports a claim that a city had organized government?
options: A necklace made from colored stones
A clay pot for storing water
A statue placed as an offering
A record of taxes ordered by a ruler
pool.rationale: A ruler collecting taxes shows government organizing resources.

pool.prompt: A tablet lists how much barley entered a storehouse. Which two characteristics does it directly show?
options: Writing and an organized food supply
pool.rationale: The written record tracks a crop in storage, connecting writing and food supply.

pool.prompt: A team finds a statue placed as an offering and a canal leading to fields. Which characteristics best match those uses?
pool.rationale: Offerings are evidence of worship, and an irrigation canal is a technology for farming.

pool.prompt: Which find most directly supports a claim about Sumerian art and craftsmanship?
options: A tax law written by a ruler
A river flowing through the lowlands
pool.rationale: A decorated cup shows the artisan’s skill and artistic choices.

pool.prompt: Two groups lived in different kinds of houses and had different duties and privileges. What does that suggest?
options: A route across the Syrian Desert
pool.rationale: Social structure describes roles, ranks, and relationships among groups.

pool.prompt: A museum wants to show how Sumerians recorded transactions. Which object belongs in that display?
options: A clay tablet with cuneiform marks
A painted statue with no inscription
A fragment of a wagon wheel
pool.rationale: Cuneiform was used to record information, including transactions.

pool.prompt: How should Ur and Sumer appear on the classroom map?
options: Ur as a star, Sumer as a dot
Ur as a dot, Sumer as a star
Both as rivers traced in blue
Both as ranges of brown triangles
pool.rationale: The map uses dots for cities and stars for the major kingdoms.

pool.prompt: Which label belongs on a blue river line?
pool.rationale: The Euphrates is one of the two major rivers named in the assignment.

pool.prompt: Which map key entry should use brown triangles?
pool.rationale: Brown triangles mark the Zagros Mountains on the classroom assignment.

pool.prompt: Which description matches the Black Land of Egypt?
pool.rationale: Kemet, or Black Land, refers to the fertile dark soil along the Nile.

pool.prompt: A boat travels downstream from near Thebes toward the Nile Delta. Where does it go?
options: South from Lower Egypt toward Upper Egypt
North from Upper Egypt toward Lower Egypt
West from Lower Egypt into the desert
East from the delta toward Thebes
pool.rationale: Upper Egypt is upstream in the south. The Nile flows north toward the delta in Lower Egypt.

pool.prompt: What is a delta, and where is Egypt’s Nile Delta?
options: Rocky rapids upstream near southern Egypt
A sandy plateau along the western desert
Land built by sediment near the river’s mouth in northern Egypt
A storage basin near a farm
pool.rationale: A delta forms as sediment collects near a river’s mouth. The Nile meets the Mediterranean in the north.

pool.prompt: Why did farmers build ditches and canals near the Nile?
options: To mark the boundaries between kingdoms
To keep the flood season from returning
pool.rationale: Canals and ditches directed water to where it was needed.

pool.prompt: Which Egyptian season name matches the time of harvest?
pool.rationale: Shemu was the harvest season. Akhet was the flood season and Peret was the growing season.

pool.prompt: Which event would fit the start of Akhet?
options: Workers harvest a ripe barley crop
The Nile begins its seasonal flood
A scribe writes on a finished scroll
pool.rationale: Akhet was the season of flooding.

pool.prompt: Who would be trained to record a grain delivery for an Egyptian official?
pool.rationale: Scribes were trained to read, write, and keep records.

pool.prompt: Which choice correctly pairs the Egyptian writing signs with a material people wrote on?
pool.rationale: Hieroglyphs are writing signs. Papyrus is a plant that Egyptians made into sheets.

pool.prompt: What would a menhed help an Egyptian worker do?
pool.rationale: The menhed was a kit of writing tools.

pool.prompt: Which ruler is commonly associated with uniting Upper and Lower Egypt?
pool.rationale: Narmer is associated with early unification. The other rulers lived much later.

pool.prompt: The same family holds Egypt’s throne across several generations. Which term fits?
pool.rationale: A dynasty is a line of rulers from the same family.

pool.prompt: Which description fits Hatshepsut?
options: The builder of the Great Pyramid
The king associated with uniting the Two Lands
The Persian ruler who captured Babylon
A pharaoh of the New Kingdom
pool.rationale: Hatshepsut was an Egyptian pharaoh during the New Kingdom.

pool.prompt: Which pair correctly identifies two Egyptian burial places?
options: Giza and Khufu’s pyramid, Valley of the Kings and Tutankhamun’s rock-cut tomb
Giza and Tutankhamun’s rock-cut tomb, Valley of the Kings and Khufu’s pyramid
Giza and Narmer’s delta, Valley of the Kings and Aswan’s quarries
Giza and Egyptian scribes’ houses, Valley of the Kings and village grain stores
pool.rationale: Khufu’s Old Kingdom pyramid is at Giza. Tutankhamun’s New Kingdom tomb is in the Valley of the Kings.

pool.prompt: Where did the granite used in Khufu’s burial chamber come from?
pool.rationale: Granite for the burial chamber was quarried at Aswan, far south of Giza.

pool.prompt: What can identifying a stone from Aswan establish on its own?
options: The exact lifting system used for the block
The exact length of the construction project
The number of people who moved the block
pool.rationale: Matching stone to a quarry gives its origin. Lifting methods require additional evidence.

pool.prompt: In the migration review, why did the Israelites first travel to Egypt?
options: Cyrus ordered them to leave Babylon
A famine threatened their food supply
pool.rationale: According to the classroom account, famine led the Israelites to Egypt.

pool.prompt: Which description matches the Exodus in biblical tradition?
options: Moses leads Israelites out of slavery in Egypt
Cyrus captures Babylon and allows return
Abraham travels from Mesopotamia to Canaan
pool.rationale: The Exodus is the departure from Egypt under Moses.

pool.prompt: Which journey is paired with its reason in biblical tradition?
options: Moses travels to Babylon to rebuild the Temple
Abraham travels toward Canaan as part of a covenant
Jacob leaves Egypt after Cyrus captures Babylon
Solomon travels to Sinai after an Assyrian attack
pool.rationale: The covenant with Abraham includes the promise associated with Canaan.

pool.prompt: How are the Torah and Tanakh related?
options: The Tanakh is the first part of the Talmud
The Torah is a place of worship
The Torah is the first part of the Tanakh
The Tanakh is another name for a synagogue
pool.rationale: The Torah forms the first part of the Tanakh, or Hebrew Bible.

pool.prompt: What does monotheism mean?
options: A ruler’s claim to a city
A group living outside its homeland
pool.rationale: Monotheism means belief in one God.

pool.prompt: Which pair is connected in the classroom account?
options: Moses and the Ten Commandments at Sinai
Saul and the capture of Babylon
Solomon and the Exodus from Egypt
Cyrus and the settlement of Canaan by Abraham
pool.rationale: In the biblical account Moses receives the commandments at Mount Sinai.

pool.prompt: What order matches the kings covered in class?
pool.rationale: Saul comes first, followed by David and then Solomon.

pool.prompt: What did Solomon build in the biblical account?
options: The synagogue in every diaspora community
pool.rationale: Solomon is credited in the biblical account with building the First Temple.

pool.prompt: After the split, where was Judah in relation to Israel?
options: North, with its capital at Nineveh
West, with its capital at Babylon
East, with its capital at Aswan
South, with its capital at Jerusalem
pool.rationale: Judah was the southern kingdom and Jerusalem was its capital.

pool.prompt: Who conquered the northern kingdom around 722 BCE?
pool.rationale: Assyria captured the northern Kingdom of Israel around 722 BCE.

pool.prompt: Which event led to the Babylonian exile?
pool.rationale: Babylon’s conquest of Judah led to exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

pool.prompt: Why did 539 BCE matter for Judean exiles?
options: Cyrus took Babylon and later permitted return
pool.rationale: Cyrus of Persia captured Babylon in 539 BCE. Return became possible under Persian rule.

pool.prompt: What is a diaspora?
options: A group of officials serving a king
People from a homeland living in communities spread elsewhere
pool.rationale: Diaspora means a population living dispersed away from its homeland.

pool.prompt: What role did synagogues play for many Jewish communities?
options: Places to gather, worship, and study
Quarries that supplied stone for homes
Palaces where Persian rulers collected taxes
pool.rationale: Synagogues supported gathering, worship, and religious learning.

pool.prompt: Which text preserves generations of rabbinic discussion?
options: The map of the Fertile Crescent
The royal record of Cyrus’s conquests
pool.rationale: The Talmud records rabbinic teaching and discussion.

dates.prompt: A label says “c. 4000 BC.” What does it mean?
dates.rationale: Circa signals an estimate. BC and BCE use the same numbering.

duration.prompt: A village grew for 50 years. How many decades is that?
duration.rationale: Fifty years divided by ten is five decades.

foragers.prompt: What would a hearth help people do on a cold evening at camp?
foragers.rationale: A hearth is a place for fire, which provides heat and can cook food.

farming.prompt: People begin planting seed from the plants that yield the most grain. What process is underway?
farming.rationale: Selecting and raising plants for useful traits is part of domestication.

economy.prompt: A village has 60 baskets of grain and needs 50 now. What are the remaining ten baskets?
economy.rationale: A surplus is what is left after current needs are met.

sumer.prompt: Which clue best supports the claim that a city could feed people after harvest time?
sumer.rationale: Stored barley could be used after the harvest ended.

sumer-art.prompt: Why is a patterned cup useful for studying culture?
options: It shows a maker’s artistic choices and skills
It lists every law in the city
It locates the mouth of the Euphrates
It gives the exact size of a harvest
sumer-art.rationale: Decoration can show craftsmanship and cultural choices.

map.prompt: How is the Fertile Crescent shown on the assignment?
options: A city marked by a dot
A mountain chain marked by triangles
map.rationale: Green identifies the Fertile Crescent region in the assigned key.

nile.rationale: Cataracts are stretches of rough water and rocks.

season.prompt: Which season comes between Akhet and Shemu?
options: The delta, at the river mouth
season.rationale: Egypt’s three seasons were flood, growth, and harvest.

writing.prompt: An official needs a written record of deliveries. Which Egyptian worker would take that assignment?
writing.rationale: Recordkeeping was a job performed by trained scribes.

egypt-rule.prompt: Why do the names Upper and Lower Egypt refer to river position?
options: Upper is upstream and Lower is downstream
Upper is north and Lower is south
Upper is west and Lower is east
Upper is in Asia and Lower is in Africa
egypt-rule.rationale: The names follow the Nile’s upstream and downstream positions.

giza.prompt: The inscription identifies the ruler buried at the Great Pyramid. Which ruler should the museum label name?
giza.rationale: The Great Pyramid was built as Khufu’s tomb.

migration.prompt: Which location is associated with the Israelites’ journey after leaving Egypt in the biblical account?
migration.rationale: The Exodus account traces a journey through Sinai.

texts.prompt: Which name means the Hebrew Bible in this unit?
texts.rationale: Tanakh is the name used for the Hebrew Bible.

kingdom.rationale: David is associated with Jerusalem as his capital.

exile.prompt: Which kingdom was conquered by Babylon, leading to exile?
exile.rationale: Babylon took Judah and sent many Judeans into exile.

diaspora.prompt: A community remains outside its homeland and keeps its traditions through study and worship. Which pairing fits?
diaspora.rationale: Diaspora describes the dispersed community. A synagogue can serve as a place of study and worship.
